entry.title: Markua graceful degradation
entry.summary: Deliberately broken Markua that shows how DocKitty degrades to readable text without failing the build.
entry.content:
Note

This page is broken on purpose. Each example below uses Markua syntax that is wrong or unsupported, to show how DocKitty handles mistakes like these.

A Markua mistake never fails the build. The page still builds, and each broken construct falls back to readable text:

  • An unknown icon is dropped, and the build log prints a warning that names it.
  • An attribute DocKitty does not support is silently ignored.
  • Syntax that cannot be paired up, such as an unclosed wrapper, stays as literal text.

For the syntax that works, see the Markua showcase.

An unknown icon drops gracefully

A callout naming an icon that is not in the seed map keeps rendering, without the icon, and the build emits a single warning naming the unknown value:

This tip names an unknown icon (fa-obscure-name). The icon is dropped with a

build warning, and the tip itself still renders.

An unsupported attribute is ignored

{fullbleed:} is not an honoured figure attribute; it is silently dropped and the image still renders:

An unbalanced wrapper stays literal

An {aside} with no matching {/aside} cannot be grouped, so its marker is left as literal text and the surrounding content renders normally — the rest of the page is not swallowed:

{aside} This paragraph follows an unterminated wrapper. The {aside} marker above renders as the literal text {aside}, and this paragraph renders as an ordinary paragraph.

Ordinary content still renders

The malformed cases above do not break anything that follows them. This closing paragraph proves the page keeps rendering to the end.
